sentences.text:
Also heard Mr. R. H.
Nabam, learned Additional Advocate General for the State respondents No.1 to 5 and Mr. T. Meto,
learned counsel appearing on behalf of Mr. M. Kato, learned Dy.S.G.I. for the respondent No.6.
2.

This writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed by the petitioners with a grievance that the petitioners belong to the Mishmi community and they are inhabitants of various villages in the proposed "Delai Reserve Forest".

However, their lands are being declared within the proposed Delai Reserve Forest which do not require any acquisition for the purpose of utilization in construction of Arunachal Pradesh Frontier Highway.

3. It is the case of the petitioners that in the year 2025, the respondent No. 3 issued a Notification dated 04.07.2025 declaring that the land falling within Km 60.000 to 121.500 of the Frontier Highway passing through the Delai proposed Reserve Forest would not require any acquisition of land.

The petitioners are aggrieved by the aforesaid Notice because the Delai proposed Reserve Forest is yet to be declared a Reserve Forest under the Assam Forest Regulation, 1891, and therefore, if any land acquisition is required to be done for the proposed Arunachal Pradesh Frontier Highway Project, that has to be done as per the law laid down under the Land Acquisition Act.
The petitioners' grievance is that by issuing the aforesaid notice, the rights of the petitioners are being sought to be Page No.# 4/5 taken away from receiving any compensation.

4. Mr. Pertin, learned counsel for the petitioners, submits that the petitioners are inhabitants of that area through which the aforesaid Arunachal Frontier Highway will pass and that, in the construction of the aforesaid road, there is a high probability that the land belonging to the petitioners would be used or utilized.
Since the land belongs to them, he therefore, submits that without properly acquiring the land, the respondent authorities should not utilize their land.
He further submits that,
vide the impugned notice

, it has been stated by the Deputy Commissioner that since the area falls under the Delai proposed Reserve Forest, no land acquisition is required to be done, which is not correct as per law, as the Delai proposed Reserve Forest is yet to be declared a reserve forest.

Therefore, any acquisition that is required to be done by the Government has to be carried out as per the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act.
5.
Mr. Nabam, learned Addl. A.G., however, submits that the petitioners have indirectly challenged the Delai proposed Reserve Forest notification issued way back in the year 1977.
However, he fairly submits that though the process of issuing the notification of the Delai proposed Reserve Forest is ongoing, the same is yet to be finalized.

6. Taking into consideration the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties,
and also keeping in mind the fact that the issue will require some consideration, let notice be issued to the respondents, returnable within 4 weeks.

7. As Mr. R. H. Nabam, learned Additional Advocate General and Mr. T. Meto, learned counsel, have entered appearance and accepted notice on behalf of Page No.# 5/5 respondents No.1 to 5 and 6 Suraj Tayang And 3 Ors vs The State Of Ap And 6 Ors on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149843190/
3 respectively, issuance of formal notice is dispensed with.

9. List the matter after four weeks.
